Now that arrays might already exist, this sort function is incorrect.  We need to now insert at the correct position, or sort the final result.  Otherwise the resulting collection order will be wrong.
added a helper called sortMembersByOdataId() to keep the result ordered. It is used both in this file and in redfish_aggregator.hpp.

getJsonArray() is also used in redfish_aggregator.hpp. I moved getJsonArrayAt() into a details namespace, while keeping getJsonArray() and getJsonArrayByPointer() unchanged.

I've updated the code. Please help review it again, thanks!

Initialize the members here?

```
    nlohmann::json::array_t& membersArr =
        getJsonArrayByPointer(asyncResp->res.jsonValue, jsonKeyName);
```

Perhaps, if getJsonArrayByPointer() is not used elsewhere, what if not use getJsonArrayByPointer() ?

```
    nlohmann::json& members = asyncResp->res.jsonValue[jsonKeyName];
    members = nlohmann::json::array();

```
and change to use `nlohmann::json& members` ?
```
inline void sortMembersByOdataId(nlohmann::json& members)
```
I've updated the code, please help review it again, thanks!
Should this be using the utility human sort function AlphanumLess?
Acknowledged

Is this place to set the empty array?
Or is the member array accumulated?
If it is an empty member, the old code seems better.
```
        asyncResp->res.jsonValue[jsonKeyName] = nlohmann::json::array();
        asyncResp->res.jsonValue[jsonCountKeyName] = 0;
```

Yes, `Members` can be accumulated in this path, so we should not reset it on io_error.

For the legacy path without the aggregator enabled, I think the old behavior would still be fine. However, when the aggregator is enabled on a platform, two response resources are merged. If we reset the array here, the entries from the aggregated response may be lost.

I don't see the nested code-paths of calling `handleCollectionMembers()`.
Could you show the cases that may accumulate Members (and which are needed)?

Sorry for the confusion - my earlier comment was not precise.

I was not referring to nested calls to handleCollectionMembers() itself. The case I had in mind is the aggregation flow, where the shared response may already contain Members entries appended by the aggregator merge path.

This is a needed case when aggregation is enabled, since valid aggregated members may already have been merged into the shared response before the local io_error path runs. Resetting Members here could then drop those previously merged entries.

Ref: https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/bmcweb/+/88012/8/redfish-core/include/redfish_aggregator.hpp#1136
Done

Is `getJsonArrayByPointer()` used/needed at the different places?
If not, I think the direct use of `getJsonArrayAt()` seems better.

```
   nlohmann::json::array_t& membersArr =
       details::getJsonArrayAt(asyncResp->res.jsonValue[jsonKeyName]);
```
Acknowledged

What should be handling if the "Members" is not an array but just an object? Looking at the code it seems like it might wipe out the non-array Members, is that intention? If so it should be tested to confirm.
Yes, that is intentional. If Members is not an array, we normalize it to an array and discard the previous non-array value. Added a test case: GetJsonArrayAtConvertsNonArrayToArray

Please also mention this is fixing a common error #13

https://github.com/openbmc/bmcweb/blob/master/docs/COMMON_ERRORS.md#13-complete-replacement-of-the-response-object

This isn't new code, and the result here is generally the mapper.  If the mapper is down, thats an internal error.

Interesting that it ends up with two duplicated entries. Is that an existing bug in handleCollectionMembers()?

(In real world we are just using the D-Bus response to report. So I can see not doing error checking for the duplicate case.)

Hi @janeta@us.ibm.com
I think this is an existing behavior in handleCollectionMembers(). Please see the logic here: https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/bmcweb/+/88012/9/redfish-core/include/utils/collection.hpp#81

If we consider this a bug, would you like me to include a fix for it in this patch as well? I will change it to use set().

At a system level getting a duplicate would be a bug in the mapper, and in theory this is an invalid input.  We could change the unit test to check A, B, and C, just to make it clear there's no duplicates, but I'm not that worried about it.  behavior is clear to me.
I'm not really worried about this one, since we are reporting what is returned from D-Bus. It just caught my eye looking at this testcase.
Remove this.  "1 hour" doesn't really describe what you tested.  Presumably you ran redfish service validator?
Updated. Yes, I ran the validator and no collection errors were found.
One minor request, then this looks good to go.
